messages:
leah: noticed a bump in 'fncall_validation' alerts this morning from retail-ingest. console flags them as failures but the downstream tool got a valid array response; schema expects an object. customers are confused.
omar: can you dump one of the examples? would like to see exact shape mismatch.
leah: logged sample: `validator_error: expected object, got array; sample='[{"sku": "X1", "qty": 2}]'` — the tool output is fine, but our adapter layer expects `{items: [...]}`. because of the strict gate we route to fallback model and increment the route's error metric.
kevin: internal note - we rolled the strict fncall gate in a small canary last night (eu-central). fallback routing to the cheaper model variant is enabled for all strict rejects.
ravi: product just pinged: they see dropped success rate and assume we lost requests, raising an SLA ticket. billing wants to know which model gets charged.
tal: current behavior: billing attribution = final_model_id (where the request executed). observability/error_count = origin_route_id's validation_rejects. so charge and error counters don't line up.
omar: that's messy. two quick fixes: 1) change console to surface a 'validated->coerced/fallback' state (not a hard error) that shows both origin and billing model; 2) change metric labels to be clearer: `validation_reject` -> `validation_event.kind=hard|soft|coercion` and `charge_model` tag for billing queries.
leah: +1 for both. product needs the console to say "Result served (fallback)" with a small amber indicator instead of full red. also include a redacted sample and a link to the request trace.
kevin: ops question: should soft/coercion events count against route quotas? some teams run strict budgeting by route. if we let them bypass quotas by falling to cheaper models, they'll see lower spend but potentially inconsistent behavior.
tal: proposal: make this configurable per-route: `fncall_shape_policy: {strict, soft, coerce}` where `soft` records an event but doesn't block; `coerce` attempts an adapter coercion (wrap array in object) and treats it as successful. default for orgs on enterprise plans = `soft`.
ravi: product: if coerce is applied, we still want visibility in billing and in SLA dashboards. display should state "coercion applied" and list origin_route and actual_execution_model.
omar: telemetry additions I propose: add tags `fallback_type` (enum: validation, timeout, capacity), `coercion_applied`=[yes/no], `origin_route_id`, `execution_model_id`, `counted_for_quota`=[yes/no]. that will let dashboards answer "how much did the canonical route actually use vs charged?"
kevin: rollout UX: we currently auto-promote fallback behaviors (if >X% validation rejects) to flip traffic to degen variant. For soft/coerce we should exclude them from auto-promotion calculations. Auto-promote should only respond to fatal rejects and capacity failures.
leah: agreed. the surprise flip this morning is what triggered product alarm.
tal: implementation notes: validator must emit machine-friendly reason codes and a `suggested_coercion` hint when possible. adapter layer should be able to do a deterministic cheap coercion (array -> {items: array}) if the route policy allows. keep coercion off by default for public plans.
ravi: billing doc note: when coercion happens, charge the execution model; but annotate the origin route for audit. product/legal want clear text in console explaining charges.
omar: monitoring change: add a new metric series `soft_fallback_rate` and a 5%/15m alert that pages SRE. but first alert to slack as a quieter notification, then page if sustained.
kevin: we also need a console panel that shows top offending routes and top shapes causing coercion so teams can fix upstream prompts.
leah: tiny UX suggestion: in the route settings page show the `fncall_shape_policy` and a one-click 'apply coercion for historical samples' for engineers to opt-in and backfill.
tal: timeline: telemetry + console display changes = 2 sprints, per-route policy + validator changes = 3 sprints, billing policy doc + legal review = 3 sprints, auto-promote exclusion = 2 sprints.
omar: action items:
- A1: telemetry tags & `soft_fallback_rate` metric (omar)
- A2: console UI state "fallback (soft/coercion)" + sample popover (leah + product)
- A3: validator reason codes + suggested_coercion (kevin)
- A4: adapter coercion path + per-route policy flag (tal)
- A5: billing/FAQ wording + legal review (ravi + finance)
- A6: monitoring alert 5%/15m with staged paging (kevin)

deploy-bot: deploy 1725551000-fncall-gating-v1 -> success (canary eu-central)

leah: I'll open the console mock PR and a support playbook for now. if anyone sees a specific route >10% soft-fallback before we finish, drop its top 3 samples here and tag @eng-oncall. :sparkles:
